avis.titre: Great but leaves a white cast.Great but leaves a white cast.
avis.texte: I bought this along with some other CeraVe products as part of skin care routine (I have acne prone sensitive skin) but I've only gotten arround to using it today so here's my review. Starting off with the good. I appreciate that it doesn't feel oily or heavy like other sunscreens I've used and that it didn't cause my skin to break out. In fact, I could've forgotten I put it on if it weren't for the typical sunscreen smell and cast it left. Plus I wore it under my makeup with no negative affects! I do have a tan skin tone and don't get sunburnt so I can't say I noticed much of a difference in how the sun affected me but I assume it did its job. As for the negatives (or rather the one negative), despite claims to the contrary it does in fact leave a white cast. Now how severe that white cast is depends on how well you rub it into your skin before it dries. Because I was in a bit of a hurry there were some areas that I didn't get properly and the white cast there was a lot more noticeable, I tried to wipe it but it had already dried so it was pointless. Luckily I wear makeup so I just covered it up but still I wouldn't recommend this if you don't have/wear makeup or are in a hurry because if you don't rub it in properly you'll get a noticeable white cast. Of course if you do it right the cast is very faint and as your skin absorbs it, it gets even less noticeable meaning that its barely a problem for most people its just that I HATE looking pale so I'll almost never wear this w

avis.titre: Reliable Daily SPF Moisturizer That Works Beautifully Under MakeupReliable Daily SPF Moisturizer That Works Beautifully
avis.texte: I’ve used this moisturizer for years and keep repurchasing it because its lightweight, non-greasy SPF 30 formula simplifies my morning routine. I started using it after having basal cell carcinoma, so daily sun protection is especially important to me. It provides effective protection while remaining comfortable for everyday wear. It absorbs quickly, delivers lasting hydration, and wears well under makeup without pilling or feeling heavy, leaving my skin smooth and protected. I originally bought it at Costco and was glad to find it on Amazon at a similar price with the convenience of Prime shipping. After years of use, it has earned a permanent place in my skincare routine. If you want a reliable daily moisturizer with sun protection that works well under makeup, this is an excellent choice.

I went through this bottle faster than I expected, which is saying something because most sunscreens annoy me enough that I abandon them halfway. This one didn’t. If you have any hyperpigmentation, sunscreen is non‑negotiable — even if you’re not planning to step outside. Yep, it matters. Indoor light still counts, and this SPF 30 makes it easy to stay consistent. The lotion absorbs quickly, doesn’t leave a greasy film, and doesn’t fight with makeup or other skincare. It’s very much a one‑and‑done morning product: moisturizer + SPF in one step. No drama, no white cast, no sticky feeling. Just simple, effective protection. I appreciate that it’s fragrance‑free, gentle, and has the classic CeraVe ceramides and hyaluronic acid. My skin didn’t complain once. Honestly? It’s the kind of product you don’t think about — you just use it every day because it works. I might add that I don't look my age. Crepey skin looks more plumped and hydrated. I have used a million and one products. I appreciate that this lotion is a decent price and does a great job.

When I used for the first time wasn't expecting to like it but turns out I do even though it seems more sunscreen than anything else. I do think they could work on the texture. I am going back to basics on my aging breakout prone skin - let's call it a reset - and this does fit the bill as a basic item. If you want anti aging punch this won't be your product but if basic simple skincare is your thing this is great. For me it's great for no makeup days and I can reapply it later in the day with no problem. Not sure why there are so many complaints about white cast...there is not that much zinc oxide in the formula seems like. At any rate this has not been a problem for me. At a later time I may advance to a more complicated anti-aging moisturizer but for now it's good.

avis.titre: Sensitive and acne prone skin people beware
avis.texte: Prior to purchasing the CeraVe Am facial moisturizer with SPF30, I was using a Cetaphil Moisturizer with SPF 50. However, as I was nearing the end of my Cetaphil moisturizer, I began to get more oily and figured I try a different moisturizer. I have also been dealing with Maskne as I’m not allowed to wear a clothe mask at the hospital I’m currently working at, even more reason why I wanted something with acne ridding ingredients. Because of that I figured I’d give the CeraVe AM moisturizer a try especially because of the active ingredients it has (I.e. niacinamide & hyaluronic acid ) as well as the positive reviews it has received on TikTok and here on Amazon. Unfortunately, within the first day my face began to feel itchy, scabby, tingly and I developed a rash all over my face. Prior to this I had been using the Paula’s Choice liquid exfoliate and my skin was smooth except for the areas with maskne. While I understand that everyone’s skin will respond differently, I’m still left with a rash and uncomfortable feeling all over my face. Also, I decided to give a 2 start rating as it began to peel when I tried to massage the moisturizer into my skin. Some positives are that this is more of a sunscreen than a moisturizer, which was what I was looking for. Also, it has no scent which is typically preferred by people with sensitive skin. I will end with the cautionary note to make sure you patch test first!! It’s been 3 days and the rash hasn’t resided.

avis.titre: A completely honest and non-paid review.
avis.texte: No, I'm not being paid for this first of all. I'll leave two different points that I consider important at the moment of choosing. One, if you are looking for a low budget skin care having only face cleaner, sun protection, moisturizer (like me) I'd say this is not the best option? Why? This product is really small, and the prize is fair because it has hialuronic acid (which if u buy it on its own is like $14) is a mixed of many good things you'd usually buy separate and is would be more expensive, so the price is excellent. BUT, you can get a nitrogena sun screen 50 fps (higher than this product's and smells amazing) for $9,99 that is farly bigger, a $16,99 rocche possay and a CeraVe daily moisturizer for $10,99 (that u can not only use in face but also body without fearing its gonna run out immediatly) and that'll last you LONGER since it's 8 ounce not only 3, I like to keep my skincare simple and affordable. Now, secondly, if the mixture is something you're interested in and can/want to afford a little more and expend more often, this is your product for sure, doesn't feel heavy on my face (i have oily face) it blends super easily and smells good, like an usual sunscreen does.

avis.titre: Not For Skin with Sunscreen Sensitivity
avis.texte: Let me start by saying, this is simply an informative warning to folks that might have skin like mine. I am an avid user of CeraVe products. It is part of my morning and nightly skincare routine. I have sensitive skin prone to dryness and love how their products interact with my skin. EXCEPT this moisturizer. My morning skincare routine consists of the hydrating facial cleanser followed by the eye repair cream, vitamin c serum, and the moisturizing lotion. However, I ran out of the moisturizing lotion and decided to give this a try. Let me preface this next part with the fact that I am notorious for having allergic reactions to sunscreen and skincare products (rashes, swelling, chemical burns, etc.) but I found and use the CeraVe hydrating sunscreen SPF 30 without complication. HOWEVER, I didn’t read the ingredients list for this product (thinking it would match the sunscreen) and there are two ingredients present in this moisturizer that I am finally beginning to understand is a no go for me: Octinoxate & Octocrylene. From what I’ve read, this sort of reaction isn't overly common for sensitive skin, but there’s alarming research none the less. Not to mention, this rash will last 3-4 days while taking Prednisone and using prescription hydrocortisone cream to deal with the itch, heat, and swelling. Again, this is just an informative review. I know and believe this product works for most as I wish it had me, but this goes for all the folks out there prone to topical reactions.
